name: Hyoscine-N-butylbromide
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Hyoscine butylbromide is a quaternary antispasmodic. Oral absolute bioavailability is under 1%, so tablets reach the circulation very little; after intravenous use about half of the dose is excreted unchanged in urine. The Canadian prescribing information does not address kidney impairment or dialysis. It has no US FDA label.
kidney_function_basis: The prescribing information does not address kidney impairment; bands shown on creatinine clearance (CrCl).

bands.recommendation: Tablets: 10 to 20 mg per dose, maximum 60 mg/day. Injection: 10 to 20 mg slowly IV, IM or SC, maximum 100 mg/day (PM).
The prescribing information gives no kidney dosing. Oral absorption is negligible; about 50% of an intravenous dose is excreted unchanged in urine. Use with caution and specialist judgment.

monitoring: Anticholinergic effects: urinary retention, tachycardia, hypotension after injection (observe; emergency equipment available), raised intraocular pressure (urgent review for painful red eye). Avoid IM injection in anticoagulated patients (PM).
